extraction_notes: Filing is intentionally generic about defense programs. The 10-K does NOT name specific Program Elements, PEs, F-35, T-7, Sentinel ICBM, NNSA, T55, F124, ATK-3000, or any other program by name. The cohort-metadata subject notes name those programs, but Honeywell's actual disclosure is at the aggregate level only: 'Defense and Space' as a business unit (revenue $7,220M FY2025) and 'U.S. Department of Defense' as a customer ($4,209M FY2025). This makes J-Book-PE-level verification IMPOSSIBLE from the filing text alone; the disclosure itself is the finding (no program-element granularity = no testable J-Book divergence claim). Claims are extracted at the level disclosed.

claims.claim_text: Honeywell Defense and Space business unit generated $7,220 million in revenue in FY2025, up from $6,091M (FY2024) and $4,986M (FY2023), within the $17,510M Aerospace Technologies segment.
claims.subject: Honeywell Defense and Space business unit

claims.claim_text: Sales to the U.S. Department of Defense were $4,209M in FY2025, $3,773M in FY2024, and $2,892M in FY2023 — DoD direct revenue grew 11.6% YoY in FY2025 and 30.5% YoY in FY2024.
claims.subject: Honeywell DoD direct sales
claims.source_quote: Sales to the U.S. Department of Defense $ 4,209 $ 3,773 $ 2,892

claims.claim_text: Honeywell does NOT expect overall 2026 operating results to be significantly affected by proposed changes in 2026 federal defense spending, citing 'varied mix of government programs' (OEM production, engineering development, aftermarket spares/repairs, overhauls) and 'diversified customer base with commercial dual-use technologies.'
claims.subject: Honeywell forward defense exposure
claims.object_value: Material insensitivity claimed; no PE/program disclosed
claims.source_quote: We do not expect our overall operating results to be significantly affected by any proposed changes in 2026 federal defense spending due to the varied mix of the government programs which impact us (OEM production, engineering development programs, aftermarket spares and repairs, and overhaul programs)

claims.claim_text: Aerospace Technologies segment carried $18,386M in backlog at December 31, 2025, out of a $37,475M total company backlog; ~57% of remaining performance obligations expected to be recognized as revenue in 2026.
claims.subject: Honeywell Aerospace Technologies backlog
claims.source_quote: Aerospace Technologies $ 18,386 ... We expect to recognize approximately 57% of our remaining performance obligations as revenue in 2026

claims.claim_text: Honeywell acquired CAES Systems Holdings LLC on Aug 30, 2024 for $1,935M, 'enhancing the Company's defense and space portfolio with high-reliability radio frequency technologies.' CAES + Civitanavi together added $485M of inorganic Aerospace sales in 2025.
claims.subject: CAES acquisition
claims.object_value: $1,935M acquisition; $485M inorganic Aero sales in 2025 (CAES+Civitanavi combined)
claims.source_quote: the Company acquired 100 % of the outstanding equity interests of CAES Systems Holdings LLC (CAES), enhancing the Company's defense and space portfolio with high-reliability radio frequency technologies, for total consideration of $ 1,935 million

claims.claim_text: Honeywell plans to complete spin-off of Honeywell Aerospace Inc. into an independent publicly-traded company in Q3 2026; Aerospace will be 'a leading global tier-1 aerospace and defense supplier of mission critical systems and technologies.'
claims.subject: Honeywell Aerospace spin-off (forward)
claims.object_value: Q3 2026 spin-off; tier-1 aerospace and defense positioning
claims.source_quote: our planned spin-off (the Spin-Off) from the Company expected to be completed in the third quarter of 2026 ... Our Honeywell Aerospace business will be a leading global tier-1 aerospace and defense supplier of mission critical systems and technologies

claims.claim_text: Aerospace Technologies 2024 Bombardier strategic agreement provides 'advanced technology for current and future Bombardier aircraft in avionics, propulsion, and satellite communications technologies' — a commercial OEM offset to DoD exposure.
claims.subject: Bombardier strategic agreement
claims.source_quote: Commercial Aviation Original Equipment business entered into a strategic agreement with Bombardier (the Bombardier Agreement) to provide advanced technology for current and future Bombardier aircraft in avionics, propulsion, and satellite communications technologies

claims.claim_text: Defense and Space business unit revenue grew $639M YoY organically in 2025, attributed to 'higher sales volume due to increased demand and shipments.'
claims.subject: Defense and Space organic growth
claims.source_quote: higher organic sales of $639 million in Defense and Space ... both driven by higher sales volume due to increased demand and shipments
